topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, setting expectations and outlining the core learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and Genetic Control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a breakdown in normal cellular differentiation, genetic regulation, and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biology and histology of tumor invasion and metastasis, using colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma progression as a primary model.

topics.label: Benign versus Malignant Tumor Behavior and Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics contrast the clinical behavior of benign and malignant tumors and outline the systematic nomenclature used to classify them.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Disease and Death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the specific mechanical, metabolic, and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Human Tissues and Animal Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across different human organ systems and in comparative animal oncology.

topics.label: Clinical Presentation and Cancer Screening Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the symptoms of cancer and evaluate the approaches, efficacy, and challenges of screening programs across major cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Practical Information
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and reminders for upcoming practicals.
